intro: A Shopify store looks more polished when every product photo feels like it came from the same shoot. Mixed backgrounds and odd crops make a collection page look unfinished, even when the products themselves are great. AIVideosUGC helps you even things out: upload the photos you have, choose a clean background or describe a setting, and get square images that sit neatly side by side.

Product pages also need something that keeps shoppers scrolling. Add a lifestyle photo, such as a throw blanket on a reading chair or a water bottle in a gym bag, and a 6, 10, 15 or 30-second video in 1:1 or 16:9 for the media gallery. Everything stays private in your account until you download it and add it in your Shopify admin. For your store's About page, team headshots in one shared setting help a small team look consistent.
tips: Use the same shape for every product photo in a collection so the grid lines up neatly.
Put your clearest, simplest photo first, because it's usually the one shown on collection pages.
Write short alt text for each image so shoppers using screen readers know what's pictured.

faq.q: What size should Shopify product photos be?
faq.a: Shopify accepts several shapes; what matters most is keeping them consistent. Our photos are square by default, which keeps collection pages tidy.

faq.q: Can I add a video to my Shopify product page?
faq.a: Yes, Shopify product media supports video. Make a 1:1 or 16:9 clip, download it, and upload it in the product's media section.

faq.q: Will all my product photos look consistent?
faq.a: Describing the same background each time helps a lot. Results can still vary slightly, so review each image before it goes on your store.

faq.q: What are Shopify product video limits?
faq.a: Shopify accepts uploaded MP4, MOV, or WebM product videos up to 10 minutes, 1 GB, and 4K (4096×2160). Our generator can export 1:1, 9:16, or 16:9; upload the version that fits your store.

overview.h2: Make a catalog feel like one store
overview.d: Shopify collection pages are easier to scan when product photos share a shape, background family, and camera height. Pick one visual rule for a collection—such as a warm neutral surface with the item centered—and repeat that rule in each prompt. AIVideosUGC creates square stills by default, which gives you a practical starting point for a tidy grid.

overview.h2: Choose media for the page job
overview.d: Use a square still as the collection anchor, then place a lifestyle image and a product-page video in the media gallery. Shopify's current limits allow images up to 5000×5000 pixels or 25 MP and under 20 MB. Uploaded product videos can be up to 10 minutes and 1 GB, up to 4K (4096×2160), in MP4, MOV, or WebM. AIVideosUGC offers 6, 10, 15, and 30 second jobs in five shapes—9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, and 3:4— with cost shown before the job starts.

items.d: Photograph each item from a comparable front or three-quarter angle so the collection grid does not jump from product to product.
Reuse a short description such as matte stone, warm daylight, and soft shadow, then change only the product and action.
Include handles, cords, lids, and the base in the source. A consistent crop cannot repair a missing component.

results.h2: A Shopify media sequence that earns its space

items.d: A square image with the product clearly isolated enough to scan beside its neighbors.
A lifestyle scene that shows where the item sits, hangs, or gets used without hiding its important parts.
A short product-page clip that demonstrates opening, packing, pouring, folding, or another visible action.

scene_recipes.h2: Scenes for collection and product pages

items.d: Place three candle vessels on the same pale wood surface with matching daylight and enough space for each label to be reviewed later.
Drape a throw blanket over a reading chair with the full weave visible and one corner falling naturally toward the floor.
A water bottle slides into an open gym bag beside a towel, then reappears on a bench for a close look.
Show a planter on a sunny sill with the pot and leaves fully in frame, leaving room for a real size note later.

after_download.h2: Load the files into Shopify with a final check

items.d: Confirm the image dimensions and file size, or the video duration, container, size, and resolution, against Shopify's current product-media guidance.
Add product names, descriptions, and alt text yourself; AI-generated lettering is not a reliable source for catalog copy.
View the new image beside the rest of the collection and adjust the crop or background when one item looks out of place.
Keep a 9:16 clip for Stories or Reels as a separate asset instead of forcing a tall crop into the product gallery.
